(3) The same test also scans all docs/**/*.md (except docs/research/) plus README.md for the whole-word phrase "MIT License" and fails if any doc contains it — new markdown docs must avoid that phrase. Unrelated aside also folded in here: new pure consumer modules under src/solar_challenge/ (e.g. community.py, finance.py) are imported by full path and are NOT re-exported in src/solar_challenge/__init__.py, so adding one needs no __init__.py edit.

content: solar_challenge test-anti-pattern convention (comprehensive code reviewer BLOCKS these at review): (1) documentation-prose substring tests — asserting a literal string is present in doc/markdown text (pins cosmetic wording/formatting, e.g. a version number); (2) markdown-surface-mirrors-`__all__` tests — asserting a docs listing equals the module's `__all__` byte-for-byte (task 82's test_consumption_doc.py did both #1 and #2 and was rejected at review; the public API is already contract-tested in tests/unit/test_init_lazy_surface.py and enforced at import time, so reference `__all__` directly rather than copying it into docs — keep doc recipes to at most a one-line prose pointer); (3) pytest structure/marker introspection meta-tests — using inspect/getattr to assert a test class exists or carries e.g. `@pytest.mark.slow` via pytestmark (rely on `pytest -m 'not slow'` collection itself instead). General discriminator, sharpened at task 107 after two guards in tests/unit/test_review_briefing.py were rejected for failing it: a guard test must assert on a REAL repository file and must survive a meaning-preserving reword of any prose it inspects — if fully rewording the text while preserving meaning breaks the test, it is a prose pin, not a behavioural check; guard a structured data class (a numeric tally, a machine-read marker token with a real consumer) instead, never repair a prose pin with a tighter regex or phrasing allow-list. Plan doc-only edits as a single impl step (no RED test).

content: solar_challenge web-assistant anthropic-import gotcha: the orchestrator's web-extra verify env (`uv run --extra dev pytest`, `uv run --extra dev mypy src/solar_challenge`, or `--extra dev --extra web`) does NOT install the anthropic SDK — even after adding it to pyproject's web extra, `uv lock` must also be run, and it can still be absent from some verify lanes. flask/plotly etc. ARE available. Consequences: (1) a module-level `import anthropic` breaks `mypy --strict` with import-not-found unless `anthropic.*` is added to `[[tool.mypy.overrides]] ignore_missing_imports` in pyproject.toml; (2) if web/assistant.py imports anthropic at module level, app.py's blueprint-registration try/except (around lines 178-185) silently re-swallows the resulting ImportError and the blueprint never registers. Rule: import anthropic LAZILY inside the function that needs it (the chat handler, slice ②) — never at module top. Leaf #35 (foundation ①) itself needs only flask and must not import anthropic at all.

content: GOTCHA (solar_challenge, observed task 111 vs 110, 2026-09-21): a follow-up task filed by an in-flight implementer is branched from the SAME base SHA as its parent, so the parent's work is NOT on the follow-up's base. Task 110 (v0.5.0 bump) and its follow-up task 111 (retarget README/briefing 0.4.0 statements) both had branch_base_sha 3f4a1c1002850783480b6d52002fc30e6458639c; 110 was still status=in-progress on branch task/110 (tip 6aaae1d) when 111's architect ran. Every "X is now stale" premise in such a follow-up is therefore FALSE at plan time and the correct exit is report_blocking_dependency on the parent, not a plan. Implementing it early inverts the drift: README would advertise 0.5.0 against a 0.4.0 pyproject/__version__ and against tests/unit/test_package.py::test_version_is_release_target. Release-tag premises are weaker still — solar-challenge-v0.5.0 is created by a HUMAN post-merge (esc-110-3), so it does not exist even immediately after the parent lands. Architects handling any "refresh stale version/tag statements after the bump" task here must verify the bump on main (git show main:pyproject.toml, git tag -l) rather than trusting the description's past-tense framing.

solar_challenge convention for giving distribution-generated homes a fleet-wide value, measured on main 460f9a1 (2026-10-08). It replaces the June task-53/69 "fleet_X keyword" convention, which task 238 overturned.
- A setting written inside fleet_distribution: lives on FleetDistributionConfig or one of its sub-configs, e.g. FleetDistributionConfig.dispatch_strategy and BatteryDistributionConfig.grid_charging / dispatch_strategy. parse_fleet_distribution_config's own parser reads it, refusing bad values at the full key path, and generate_homes_from_distribution reads it from the config. Do not add a fleet_X keyword to the generator.
- A top-level block of the fleet file (today only tariff:) is read by config._read_fleet_distribution_file and passed on by _FleetFileSettings.generate_homes. That is the one place that decides which top-level blocks generated homes get (task 315), and the generator's fleet_tariff keyword exists for it.
- The generator's fleet_grid_charging / fleet_dispatch_strategy keywords have no production caller. Task 335 retires them; they are gone once 335 merges.
- Calibration safety: scenarios/bristol-fin-calibration.yaml has no top-level tariff:, grid_charging or dispatch_strategy, so every such value must default to None.
